798 ## Replacing text in a TipTap block: use `element.editor`, not the clipboard (30 Jul) 799 800 The single most useful Squarespace-automation finding so far. Every `.tiptap.ProseMirror` 801 element **exposes its TipTap Editor instance as `element.editor`**, so a whole block's 802 content can be replaced in one call that cannot append, cannot half-apply, and preserves 803 whatever classes you pass: 804 805 ```js 806 const eds = [...frameDoc.querySelectorAll('.tiptap.ProseMirror')]; 807 eds[0].editor.commands.setContent( 808 '

TITLE

', true); 809 eds[1].editor.commands.setContent(paras.map(t => 810 `

${t}

` 811 ).join(''), true); 812 ``` 813 814 The second argument (`emitUpdate = true`) is what marks the page dirty so SAVE enables. 815 Keep Squarespace's own `class` / `style` / `data-rte-preserve-empty` attributes in the HTML 816 you pass - that is what makes the result visually identical to hand-typed content. 817 818 **Four approaches that failed first. Do not re-try them:** 819 820 1. **`innerHTML = ...`** - ProseMirror ignores DOM mutations entirely; nothing registers. 821 2. **DOM range (`getSelection().addRange`) + synthetic `ClipboardEvent('paste')`** - 822 ProseMirror keeps its **own** selection state and ignores the DOM selection, so the 823 paste lands at the cursor and the old content survives *underneath* the new. This is 824 the dangerous one: the block looks correct in a truncated `innerText` check while 825 actually holding both copies. It silently corrupted two pages. 826 3. **Real `Control+A` via CDP `press_key`, then paste** - works only when the preceding 827 CDP click genuinely focused that specific editor, which is unreliable across pages. 828 Diagnose it by reading `getSelection().toString().length` before pasting: 51 chars = 829 the heading was focused correctly, 1192 chars = the body block was focused instead. 830 It also left trailing nodes on multi-paragraph blocks even when the selection was right. 831 4. **`Control+A` then `Backspace` on a single-line HEADING block - destructive.** Emptying 832 a one-line block deletes **the block itself**, taking the page from 3 blocks to 2 and 833 breaking the template. Recoverable only because it was never saved. 834 835 **Always verify before clicking SAVE.** Assert the heading equals the intended title, and 836 that the body no longer matches a signature of the old copy (e.g. 837 `/flat-pack furniture|free quotation/`). That guard caught every failure above and is the 838 only reason nothing bad was ever persisted: 839 840 ```js 841 if (!headOk || !bodyOk) return {saved: false, ...diagnostics}; // do NOT click SAVE 842 ``` 843 844 **To discard a bad edit, navigate away without saving.** A `beforeunload` dialog appears - 845 accept it. The last saved state reloads clean; verified. 846 847 ## Retargeting a Button block's link and label (5 Aug) - it IS scriptable

Every `.tiptap.ProseMirror` element **exposes its TipTap Editor instance as `element.editor`**, so a whole block's content can be replaced in one call that cannot append, cannot half-apply, and preserves whatever classes you pass: ```js const eds = [...frameDoc.querySelectorAll('.tiptap.ProseMirror')]; eds[0].editor.commands.setContent( '

TITLE

', true); eds[1].editor.commands.setContent(paras.map(t => `

${t}

` ).join(''), true); ``` The second argument (`emitUpdate = true`) is what marks the page dirty so SAVE enables. Keep Squarespace's own `class` / `style` / `data-rte-preserve-empty` attributes in the HTML you pass - that is what makes the result visually identical to hand-typed content. **Four approaches that failed first. Do not re-try them:** 1. **`innerHTML = ...`** - ProseMirror ignores DOM mutations entirely; nothing registers. 2. **DOM range (`getSelection().addRange`) + synthetic `ClipboardEvent('paste')`** - ProseMirror keeps its **own** selection state and ignores the DOM selection, so the paste lands at the cursor and the old content survives *underneath* the new. This is the dangerous one: the block looks correct in a truncated `innerText` check while actually holding both copies. It silently corrupted two pages. 3. **Real `Control+A` via CDP `press_key`, then paste** - works only when the preceding CDP click genuinely focused that specific editor, which is unreliable across pages. Diagnose it by reading `getSelection().toString().length` before pasting: 51 chars = the heading was focused correctly, 1192 chars = the body block was focused instead. It also left trailing nodes on multi-paragraph blocks even when the selection was right. 4. **`Control+A` then `Backspace` on a single-line HEADING block - destructive.** Emptying a one-line block deletes **the block itself**, taking the page from 3 blocks to 2 and breaking the template. Recoverable only because it was never saved. **Always verify before clicking SAVE.** Assert the heading equals the intended title, and that the body no longer matches a signature of the old copy (e.g. `/flat-pack furniture|free quotation/`). That guard caught every failure above and is the only reason nothing bad was ever persisted: ```js if (!headOk || !bodyOk) return {saved: false, ...diagnostics}; // do NOT click SAVE ``` **To discard a bad edit, navigate away without saving.** A `beforeunload` dialog appears - accept it.
